business_problem: Aurasell's AI agents and dashboards generate roughly 300 to 400 queries per second, but its traditional data warehouse averaged one-to-two-second query times and required multiple clusters for concurrency. Copying data to a separate serving system risked silos, inconsistent answers, and restricted joins.
solution_summary: Aurasell keeps its data in the Databricks Lakehouse and uses Lakehouse//RT as the real-time serving tier for AI agents and in-product dashboards. The team routes 80% of analytics and data-discovery queries to Lakehouse//RT; a single cluster handles 300 concurrent queries that previously required multiple warehouse clusters. Unity Catalog governs the shared data copy, so agents can join tables without replicating hot data into an external serving store. Unity Gateway handles AI model routing on the same platform. This avoids data migration and a separate serving layer while supporting millisecond query response. The source does not identify the upstream systems feeding the lakehouse or the exact ingestion implementation.

data_flow: Aurasell keeps its data in the Databricks Lakehouse; AI model requests are routed through Unity Gateway, while analytics and data-discovery queries from agents and in-product dashboards go to Lakehouse//RT. Unity Catalog governs the shared data copy that agents query directly, avoiding replication to an external serving store.
business_outcome: Aurasell reduced real-time serving costs by 7x, achieved query latency of 50 to 300 milliseconds at p90 depending on workload, and eliminated the separate real-time serving layer while keeping agents on one governed copy of data.
